title: Jailer 2's Telugu Bet: ₹45 Crore Rights, a Slow Start and a Weekend to Save It
excerpt: Rajinikanth's sequel is a blockbuster in Tamil but opened soft in the Telugu states, where Naga Vamsi's Sithara paid about ₹45 crore for rights. Trade estimates put day one in the Telugu states at ₹15 crore-plus, against a recovery target trade pegs at ₹80-90 crore of collections.
body:
• Jailer 2's Tamil version is performing at blockbuster level, but its Telugu version has opened slowly despite decent-to-positive word of mouth, 123Telugu reported.
  • Telugu distribution rights sold for about ₹45 crore to producer Naga Vamsi; trade estimates say recovery needs roughly ₹80-90 crore in collections.
  • Trade trackers estimated day one at about ₹130 crore worldwide, with the Telugu states contributing ₹15 crore-plus — a start that leaves the Telugu bet dependent on weekend growth.
  • North America mirrors the Telugu pattern, according to 123Telugu; the territory's break-even is about $7 million, against the first Jailer's $6.83 million lifetime gross there.

Rajinikanth is back as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian, and in Tamil the sequel is doing what sequels are supposed to do. In the Telugu states, the market that paid one of the richest prices for the film, Jailer 2 has started slowly — and the gap between the two stories is now the film's central box-office question, according to 123Telugu.

The price of the bet

Producer Naga Vamsi reportedly acquired the Telugu states theatrical rights for about ₹45 crore, with overseas rights — held by Shloka Entertainments across North America, the UK, Europe, Africa, Sri Lanka and Nepal — valued at about ₹47.5 crore, taking the combined Telugu-plus-overseas value past ₹90 crore, Gulte reported before release. Trade estimates put the Telugu recovery requirement at roughly ₹80-90 crore in collections — a demanding target for a dubbed Tamil film, however large the star.

Day one, in numbers

Track Tollywood's day-one estimates show both halves of the story. Worldwide, the Nelson Dilipkumar film was heading for about ₹130 crore gross, the third-biggest Kollywood opening ever, with Tamil Nadu at about ₹25 crore, Karnataka ₹14 crore-plus and Kerala ₹12 crore-plus — and the Telugu states at ₹15 crore-plus. The pattern inside the day matters: noon shows started slowly after a quiet pre-release campaign, and collections more than doubled by the night shows as positive word of mouth spread, the same climb the first Jailer made in 2023. Official figures from Sun Pictures will settle the estimates.

https://x.com/123telugu/status/2111131570308624681

The diaspora mirror

123Telugu reported the situation is similar in North America, where the rights were valued at ₹28 crore and break-even sits at about $7 million — a figure the first Jailer nearly reached on its own, grossing $6.83 million over its lifetime in the territory. For US and Canadian audiences, that makes this a familiar Rajinikanth weekend: the film does not need a record opening, it needs the word-of-mouth curve that doubled its Friday by nightfall to keep bending upward through Sunday.

What happens next

The Telugu verdict now rests on the weekend. If the dubbed version follows the Tamil trajectory, the ₹45 crore rights price becomes a footnote; if the slow start hardens, Jailer 2 becomes the rare Rajinikanth film that is simultaneously a blockbuster and a distribution loss — separated only by language.
